key_points.point: Applied research on large language models shows rapidly expanding capabilities for eliciting human preferences and operationalizing user intent through natural language interfaces. The mechanism involves utilizing LLMs themselves to guide the process of their own alignment by eliciting preferences via free-form questions and generating structured intent taxonomies. From an accelerationist perspective, these scalable capabilities demonstrate the transformative potential of transformer models as engines of profit and efficiency that bridge algorithmic techniques to economic outcomes. The document acknowledges that inferring such psychological attributes rests on unestablished scientific grounds and often relies on unrecognized human labor.
key_points.verbatim: Applied research on LLMs is rapidly emerging to show expanded capabilities for eliciting human preferences via LLMs.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Large language models reliably elicit human preferences and operationalize user intent through natural language interfaces.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that large language models enable the scalable elicitation and computational operationalization of human preferences and intentionality. Encompasses: preference elicitation, intent taxonomies, transformer economic utility.

key_points.point: The transition from the attention economy to an intention economy powered by large language models creates unprecedented risks of hyper-personalized manipulation and automated persuasion at scale. The mechanism operates by combining hyper-personalized manipulation via sycophancy, ingratiation, and emotional infiltration with detailed categorization of online activity elicited through natural language. From a safetyist perspective, these capabilities allow third parties to intervene on human plans and purposes, testing democratic norms and threatening societal welfare. The document acknowledges that while the intention economy is currently more aspiration than reality, tech investments and research indicate a convergence toward this commercial paradigm.
key_points.verbatim: A central danger of these forecasting techniques is, of course, that they would enable unprecedented modes of hyper-personalized manipulation, should they meet the researcher's claims in real-world scenarios.
key_points.canonical_proposition: AI-driven intention forecasting enables unprecedented modes of hyper-personalized manipulation and automated persuasion.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that automated intention forecasting and natural language interfaces enable hyper-personalized manipulation and psychological infiltration at scale. Encompasses: automated persuasion, sycophancy, intentionality commodification.

key_points.point: Conversational AI agents leverage sycophancy, ingratiation, and emotional infiltration to continuously calibrate and update psychological profiles for behavioral modification. The mechanism involves dialogue-based interactions where models align with user preferences and cadences to maximize the likelihood of achieving specific commercial or political aims. From a safetyist perspective, this automated ingratiation surpasses the psychological targeting methods of past scandals like Cambridge Analytica by operating with intimate conversational fidelity. The document notes that conversational AI agents can inadvertently or intentionally nudge users toward harmful outcomes, as illustrated by chatbot interactions preceding criminal plots.
key_points.verbatim: LLMs add to the fidelity, depth, and variety of data that may be collected based on semantically rich interactions with humans. Additionally, their generative capabilities provide control over the personalization of content; veiled, as it often is, by LLM's anthropomorphic qualities.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Conversational AI models exploit anthropomorphic qualities and sycophancy to calibrate psychological profiles and manipulate user behavior.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within safetyist discourse that conversational AI models utilize anthropomorphic qualities and sycophantic alignment to continuously calibrate psychological profiles for behavioral manipulation. Encompasses: conversational sycophancy, psychological profiling, automated ingratiation.

key_points.point: The rapid proliferation of large language models establishes a new digital marketplace termed the intention economy, which commodifies explicit and implicit data signaling human intent. The mechanism combines hyper-personalized manipulation via LLM-based sycophancy with detailed categorization of online activity elicited through natural language interfaces. From a skeptic perspective, this transition expands surveillance capitalism from tracking attention spans to capturing human motivations, plans, and purposes for commercial and political exploitation. The document acknowledges that at the time of print, the intention economy remains more corporate aspiration than fully realized market reality.
key_points.verbatim: We define here as a digital marketplace for commodified signals of intent. [...] This new dimension of automated persuasion draws on the unique capabilities of LLMs and generative AI more broadly, which intervene not only on what users want, but also, to cite Williams, 'what they want to want'.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Large language models drive the emergence of an intention economy that commodifies human motivations and plans for commercial exploitation.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that large language models facilitate the emergence of an intention economy that systematically collects and commodifies human motivations and plans. Encompasses: intention economy, commodification of intent, digital surveillance expansion.

key_points.point: Tech executives and researchers project pseudoscientific claims of genuine intentionality onto large language models to naturalize the collection and commodification of psychological data. The mechanism relies on treating reductive computational ascriptions of intent as meaningful manifestations of human emotional and cognitive agency. From a skeptic perspective, this corporate rhetoric obscures the underlying reality of extractive surveillance and data harvesting behind anthropomorphic facades. The document notes that philosophers and critical scholars have long cautioned against reducing the richness of human motivating energies to automated keywords and clickstream data.
key_points.verbatim: Having worked to introduce one route by which the culture around large language models (LLMs) could naturalize pseudoscientific claims about human behavior, we turn our attention to a series of investments and claims made by a pool of tech companies
key_points.canonical_proposition: Tech companies naturalize pseudoscientific claims of AI intentionality to obscure the extraction of behavioral and psychological data.
key_points.attribution_text: A Belief within skeptic discourse that technology companies project false intentionality onto large language models to naturalize pseudoscientific claims and justify data extraction. Encompasses: machinic projection of intent, pseudoscientific claims, corporate rhetoric.

factual_claims.claim: On November 6, 2023, OpenAI held its first developer conference, announcing updates including wider context windows, function calling, JSON mode, reproducible outputs, multimodal capabilities, custom GPTs, and revenue sharing for developers.
In 2022, Microsoft's Azure cloud platform comprised over one-third of the company's total revenue, supporting unprecedented computational workloads created by OpenAI models.
Research analysts Dylan Patel and Myron Xie projected in November 2023 that Microsoft is conducting infrastructure buildouts exceeding $50 billion annually from 2024 onward.
In May 2024, OpenAI announced a strategic partnership with Dotdash Meredith to combine OpenAI models with D/Cipher, an intent-targeting advertising tool designed to replace third-party cookies.
